disclaimer: HYPOTHETICAL. Stripe has not proposed or announced this change. Shockwave's team created this scenario to demonstrate impact analysis. Stripe is not a Shockwave customer and has not endorsed Shockwave.
old_semantics: USD amount in minor currency units (cents): 1000 represents $10.00
new_semantics: USD amount in major currency units (dollars): 10 represents $10.00

structural_schema.note: The proposed contract keeps Stripe's published schema byte-for-byte (amount stays integer). A units change is invisible to a schema diff; the analyzer learns the new semantics only from this manifest.

bounded_example_limits: The fixtures use whole-dollar USD values (10, 4000, 5000, 6000) so the proposed values still satisfy the published integer type.
This bounded example does not establish a practical general major-unit representation: fractional dollars (e.g. $10.99) cannot be expressed as an integer in major units.
The scenario covers USD only; zero-decimal and three-decimal currencies, and other amount fields (amount_received, amount_capturable, ...), are out of scope.
Stripe documents a minimum charge amount and an eight-digit amount limit in minor units; the hypothetical does not re-derive those limits.
